title: Exploring a kinase inhibitor targeting PI3KCA mutant cancer cells.
authors: AlKharboush, Dana F; Khayat, Maan T; Jamal, Alam; El-Araby, Moustafa E; Awaji, Aeshah A; Khan, Mohammad Imran; Omar, Abdelsattar M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子激酶抑制剂KIM-161靶向PI3KCA突变癌细胞，核心是蛋白-小分子互作，与蛋白质-DNA互作及TF-DNA结合体系无关。
abstract: The PI3K/mTOR signaling pathway is often disrupted in human cancers, with PI3Kalpha being one of the most mutated kinases. There has been considerable interest in developing small-molecule inhibitors aimed at blocking the mutant PI3Kalpha-driven phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) signaling pathway as a potential treatment for cancer. In this study, we describe our effort to identify a compound, phenylacetamide-1H-imidazol-5-one (KIM-161), from our in-house oncogenic kinase-targeting inhibitors. KIM-161 showed excellent anti-proliferative activities at sub-nanomolar concentrations, primarily against mutant PI3Kalpha breast cancer cell lines, when compared with wild-type PI3Kalpha breast cancer cell lines, producing both dose- and time-dependent effects with an IC50 range of 1.42 - 0.064 microM. Next, we observed that KIM-161 was able to induce ROS production by modulating breast cancer metabolism, suggesting its broad effects on mutant PI3Kalpha regulated downstream pathways. We also computationally analyzed the binding interactions between KIM-161 and PI3K-alpha (PDB ID: 8EXL). Molecular docking showed that KIM-161 had a docking score of -7.44 Kcal/mol, compared to the reference compound, which had a docking score of -7.67 Kcal/mol. Moreover, molecular dynamics simulation studies demonstrated that the PI3Ka-KIM-161 complex remained stable throughout the 100 ns simulation, when compared to the PI3Ka complex with the co-crystallized inhibitor. These findings present KIM-161 as a promising lead, providing valuable insights into treatment approaches and resistance mechanisms associated with PI3K inhibitors in specific PIK3CA-mutant cancer subtypes.
abstract_zh: PI3K/mTOR信号通路在人类癌症中经常发生紊乱，其中PI3Kalpha是突变最频繁的激酶之一。开发旨在阻断突变型PI3Kalpha驱动的磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）信号通路的小分子抑制剂，作为癌症的潜在治疗方法，一直备受关注。在本研究中，我们描述了从我们内部靶向致癌激酶的抑制剂库中鉴定出一种化合物——苯乙酰胺-1H-咪唑-5-酮（KIM-161）的努力。与野生型PI3Kalpha乳腺癌细胞系相比，KIM-161在亚纳摩尔浓度下表现出优异的抗增殖活性，主要针对突变型PI3Kalpha乳腺癌细胞系，产生剂量和时间依赖性效应，IC50范围为1.42至0.064微摩尔。接下来，我们观察到KIM-161能够通过调节乳腺癌代谢诱导ROS产生，表明其对突变型PI3Kalpha调控的下游通路具有广泛影响。我们还通过计算分析了KIM-161与PI3K-alpha（PDB ID: 8EXL）之间的结合相互作用。分子对接显示，KIM-161的对接分数为-7.44 Kcal/mol，而参考化合物的对接分数为-7.67 Kcal/mol。此外，分子动力学模拟研究表明，与共结晶抑制剂的PI3Ka复合物相比，PI3Ka-KIM-161复合物在100 ns模拟期间保持稳定。这些发现将KIM-161呈现为一个有前景的先导化合物，为特定PIK3CA突变癌症亚型中与PI3K抑制剂相关的治疗方法和耐药机制提供了宝贵见解。
